intro.heading: You give your time. We carry the workload.
paragraphs: As a director of a resident management company (RMC) or a right to manage (RTM) company, you're usually a volunteer leaseholder. You give your time for free, but you carry legal duties: company law, fire safety, health and safety and the terms of the leases.

Belgarum Property Management is a managing agent: a firm the board employs to run the building day to day. We do the work that helps you meet your duties. Your board keeps the decisions, and you get one dedicated property manager as your contact.

included.heading: What we take off your board
items: Day-to-day management of the building and communal areas
Service charge budgets, collection and credit control
Company secretary duties for RMCs, including Companies House returns and annual general meetings (AGMs)
Fire risk, asbestos and health and safety assessments, through specialist firms
[Section 20 consultation](/services/section-20-consultation/) (the legal process for consulting leaseholders) before major works
Enforcement of lease covenants, the promises each leaseholder makes in their lease
Regular site inspections, and management reports for larger developments

steps.title: One contact for the board
steps.text: Your dedicated property manager is the board's main contact, Monday to Thursday, 9am to 5pm, and Friday, 9am to 4.30pm.

steps.title: We advise, you decide
steps.text: We prepare budgets, get prices and recommend actions. The board makes the decisions, such as agreeing the budget or choosing a contractor.

steps.title: We do the work
steps.text: We collect the service charge, arrange repairs and assessments, run consultations and keep the company's records.

steps.title: You stay informed
steps.text: Your property manager inspects the building regularly. Larger developments also get regular management reports.

proof: We can manage the building and act as your company secretary, so the board deals with one firm.
Switching agents? We handle the handover from your current agent, including the records, funds and contracts.
Your building's money sits in its own trust account, never mixed with ours or with another building's.
Our own Code of Conduct sets time limits for replying to the board.

faqs.question: What is the difference between an RMC and an RTM company?
answer: An RMC is a company, usually owned by the leaseholders, that is responsible under the leases for managing the building or estate.
An RTM company is set up by leaseholders to take over the management of their building from the freeholder, using a legal right. The freeholder still owns the building.

faqs.question: Do directors keep their legal duties if they appoint a managing agent?
answer: Yes. Directors keep their duties under the Companies Act 2006, and the company keeps its duties under the leases and safety law. A managing agent does the work that helps the board meet those duties, and has duties of its own for the work its contract covers. For advice on your own position, take independent legal advice.

faqs.question: How do we move to BPM from our current managing agent?
answer: Check your current management agreement for its notice period. The board then decides when to give notice. We then arrange the handover with your current agent, including the building's records, service charge funds and contracts.
To compare us with your current agent, [request a management proposal](/contact/?type=new-management). It sets out what we would do for your building.

faqs.question: Do you manage buildings for RTM companies?
answer: We manage buildings for RTM companies once they have taken over management. Since 3 March 2025, the RTM company and its members do not usually pay the freeholder's costs of a claim. A tribunal can still order costs in some cases, such as a claim withdrawn unreasonably. An RTM claim is also possible where up to 50% of the building is not residential. For advice on making a claim, take independent legal advice.

faqs.question: What does the board still decide?
answer: The big decisions stay with the board. These include agreeing the service charge budget, choosing contractors for major works, and deciding how to enforce the leases. We give you the information and advice to make those decisions.
